description: Three times a specificity argument was tested against simply using all the data, and three times using everything won: restricting training screens to the matching question type, compressing the co-occurrence statistics, and restricting the atlas to the matching tissue. Each restriction is individually plausible and each loses to sample size, by a factor of 6 to 13 in the one case measured both ways. This is a genuine finding about this problem rather than three unrelated nulls.
metric: 3 independent restriction experiments
value: all three worse than using everything
verdict: RULE - use everything

method: RULE: a feature must be pointed by the screen's own results, not by a lookup
description: The one property that separates the method that works from the nine that do not. The successful feature does not predict anything by itself - it supplies a way of measuring which genes behave similarly, and the screen's OWN confirmed hits choose the direction to search in. Every feature that instead arrives as a fixed opinion about each gene has failed: a language model's gene scores, baseline gene expression, transcriptional response, drug-sensitivity correlation, and same-drug screen transfer. The cleanest demonstration is that the SAME underlying gene-deletion data works when pointed by the screen's hits and gives nothing at all when pointed by the screen's drug name instead.
metric: 5 fixed-opinion features vs 1 results-pointed feature
value: all five fail; the results-pointed one is the deployed method
verdict: RULE - ask what a candidate does with the hits already confirmed

method: GATE: does the data cover the genes you need to rank?
description: The cheapest of the three pre-screens and the only structural one - you cannot rank genes you have no values for, whatever the quality of the signal. Reference coverage of each screen's hits: gene-deletion atlas 83% of all genes, protein interactions 61%, overexpression morphology 56%, transcriptional response 46%, and the overexpression signature atlas 13.5%, which is what ruled the last one out for an 11 MB download instead of 2 GB. This gate was skipped for three successive recommendations of that atlas before anyone applied it.
metric: a PRE-SCREEN gate, not an EF result: a structural property a candidate feature must have before its margin means anything (see the '6. Method and gates' group)
value: below roughly 40% coverage a feature cannot help
verdict: GATE - check this BEFORE recommending a feature

method: GATE: is the feature just rediscovering famous genes?
description: A feature that correlates with how often a gene is a hit in general is probably telling the model something it already encodes, which is how a language model's gene scores could separate hits from non-hits and still add exactly nothing. Measured as the correlation between the candidate feature and each gene's overall hit frequency across 1,349 screens. Drug-sensitivity correlation passes cleanly at about 0.00; protein-interaction connectivity is borderline at +0.20, since well-connected proteins are also better studied; same-drug screen transfer fails badly at +0.60.
metric: a PRE-SCREEN gate, not an EF result: a structural property a candidate feature must have before its margin means anything (see the '6. Method and gates' group)
verdict: GATE - a fame-correlated feature is probably redundant

method: GATE: does the data carry any functional signal at all?
description: A positive control, and the one that produced the most interesting negative in the project. Before believing that a dataset has nothing to offer, check that genes known to work together - members of the same protein complex - actually look similar in it. This exists because one atlas once scored exactly at chance, which looked like a clean null and was in fact 6,832 corrupted values being silently converted to astronomically large numbers. It later showed that the overexpression morphology atlas genuinely carries no such signal, which is a far more informative result than its weak score alone.
metric: a PRE-SCREEN gate, not an EF result: a structural property a candidate feature must have before its margin means anything (see the '6. Method and gates' group)
value: co-complex genes 4-11 sd above random pairs in the working atlas; 0 sd in overexpression morphology
verdict: GATE - read this before trusting any null
